kinds.d: Miniature wall-mounted household altar enshrining a kami, usually with a mirror and ofuda.

x.d: Small shrine mounted high on a wall; the shintai is most often a small round mirror, with ofuda and offerings of water, sake or food.
x.dt: wood · mirror · ofuda · mizutama water vessel

kinds.d: Talisman of paper, wood, cloth or metal issued by a shrine or temple and kept on a household altar.

x.d: Talisman issued by the Ise Grand Shrines, a wooden tablet with a cedar sliver wrapped in paper; often the first placed on a household altar.
x.dt: wooden tablet · cedar sliver (gyoshin) · paper wrapper

kinds.d: Small charm carried, not worn as jewellery, for luck, protection or a named blessing. A worn one is in Jewellery; one issued for money is in Coins, Stamps, Medals & Trading Cards.

x.d: Amulet sold at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples, usually a brocade silk bag enclosing a paper or wood prayer; replaced yearly.
x.dt: brocade bag · paper or wood inside

x.d: Eye-shaped handmade glass amulet, blue and white, against the evil eye.
Palm-shaped amulet against the evil eye, often with an eye motif, worn or hung on walls.

kinds.d: Wooden plaque on which a wish is written, left at a shrine; the other side bears a picture.
Paper fortune slip drawn at a shrine or temple for a small offering.
Wand of zigzag paper or metal-foil streamers set at a shrine or household altar as the sign of the kami's presence (gohei, kinpei named forms).
Rope hung to mark a sacred space or object in a rite. A seasonal festival decoration such as the kadomatsu is in Decor.
Lantern made to be hung or set out in a rite or as a shrine offering. A garden stone lantern or decorative lantern is in Decor; a lantern made to be carried as a light is in Lighting.

notes: Chochin not covered. Ichisha/sansha not on the Kamidana page (listed as types only).
